facts.text: The study varied V content from 0 at.% in W44Ta56 to 3 at.% in W53Ta44V3 and 5 at.% in W53Ta42V5.
The films were irradiated in situ with 1 MeV Kr ions to approximately 20 dpa.
Before irradiation, the films were annealed at 1173 K for 10 min.
Kr irradiation was conducted at 1073 K for 1 h with a flux of 1.25×10^12 ions cm^-2 s^-1 and a fluence of 4.50×10^15 ions cm^-2.
The 5 at.% V alloy exhibited weaker negative high-temperature Ta–V and W–V chemical short-range order and a more homogeneous atomic distribution than the 3 at.% V alloy.
V additions reduced self-interstitial mobility relative to binary W–Ta, bringing interstitial and vacancy mobilities closer together and thereby increasing defect recombination.
Enhanced defect recombination suppressed the formation of large interstitial clusters that would otherwise leave excess vacancies available for void formation.
Both V-containing alloys retained nanocrystalline BCC morphologies without detectable irradiation-driven grain growth after irradiation to approximately 20 dpa.
W53Ta42V5 showed no detected irradiation-induced segregation or precipitation, whereas W53Ta44V3 exhibited grain-boundary W enrichment and Ta depletion.
Increasing V to 5 at.% produced smaller voids than either the 3 at.% V alloy or the V-free W44Ta56 comparator.
Mean void diameters were 2.37±0.01 nm in W44Ta56, 1.65±0.01 nm in W53Ta44V3, and 1.19±0.01 nm in W53Ta42V5.
Reported void areal densities were 1.8±0.2×10^-2 nm^-2 for W44Ta56, 1.3±0.1×10^-1 nm^-2 for W53Ta44V3, and 8.3±0.8×10^-2 nm^-2 for W53Ta42V5.
